## Paper

Autonomous algorithmic collusion: Q-learning under sequential pricing

## World

pricing_arena

## Institution

Pricing timing/protocol choice.

## Agent type

Q-learning pricing firms.

## Theoretical benchmark

Sequential versus simultaneous pricing changes strategic observability and punishment opportunities.

## Learning setup

Repeated pricing with a specific move protocol; interpretation depends on timing.

## Metrics

Average prices, profit, collusion index, learning dynamics.

## Main result

Competing Q-learning algorithms in a sequential pricing environment can converge to collusive equilibria, achieving supra-competitive profits. The results are robust to various extensions and demonstrate the potential for autonomous algorithmic collusion.

## What they prove

Q-learning algorithms can converge to collusive equilibria in a sequential pricing environment; the results are robust to various extensions

## What they only simulate

Convergence to collusive equilibria; the coordination problem in algorithmic collusion

## What they do NOT test

Real-world implementation of pricing algorithms; legal and regulatory implications of algorithmic collusion

## What we need to reproduce

State explicitly that Pricing Arena uses simultaneous action semantics unless a sequential variant is implemented.

## How our project differs

The paper studies sequential pricing. This repo's current pricing world is simultaneous, so the paper is a timing caveat and future-ablation anchor.
